blocks.t: **Objetivo de comunicação (C2):** eu consigo ler, ouvir, falar e escrever sobre a vida e a obra de uma pensadora a partir de uma biografia, apresentando fatos com entonação adequada.

body: Esta aula treina **responder em frases completas (IELTS Speaking, TOEFL Speaking)**.

blocks.t: Toque em 🔊, ouça e repita cada palavra. Depois tente adivinhar o sentido.

blocks.name: Hannah Arendt
paras: Hannah Arendt was born in 1906 in Linden, near Hanover, Germany, and **studied** philosophy under Martin Heidegger and Karl Jaspers, **completing** her doctorate in 1929. After the Nazis **came to power**, she **left** Germany in 1933; in 1941 she **reached** the United States, where she **remained** for the rest of her life.

Her book *The Origins of Totalitarianism* (1951) **made her name**, and *The Human Condition* (1958) **explored** labour, work and action. She **covered** the 1961 trial of Adolf Eichmann for *The New Yorker*; the resulting book **introduced** the phrase “**the banality of evil**”, which **provoked** fierce debate that **has not abated**.
Arendt **taught** at several universities and **died** in New York in 1975.
facts: The Origins of Totalitarianism; The Human Condition; Eichmann in Jerusalem

items.q: Arendt emigrated to the United States in 1941.
items.why: in 1941 she reached the United States.

items.q: Arendt wrote poetry as a child.
The debate over “the banality of evil” has ended.

blocks.body: Biografias combinam **passado simples** (eventos), **particípios** (ações ligadas) e **presente perfeito** (efeitos que duram). Datas: *in 1951*, *between… and…*.
*Born* é adjetivo-participial: *She was born in 1906*, nunca *She borned*.

items.s: ___ her doctorate in 1929, she studied philosophy. (complete, -ing)
The phrase provoked debate that ___ not abated. (have)

blocks.title: Match the word to its meaning

body: **Make one’s name** — fazer nome
**Leave a legacy** — deixar um legado
**Come to power** — chegar ao poder
**Stand the test of time** — resistir ao tempo
**Break new ground** — abrir novos caminhos
**Spark a debate** — gerar debate
**Reach a wide audience** — alcançar um grande público
**Go into exile** — exilar-se
**In one’s own right** — por mérito próprio
**Bear witness** — dar testemunho
**When did Arendt leave Germany?** — Quando Arendt deixou a Alemanha?
**In 1933, after the Nazis came to power.** — Em 1933, depois que os nazistas chegaram ao poder.
**What did she write about the Eichmann trial?** — O que ela escreveu sobre o julgamento de Eichmann?

forms: Ela expôs sua teoria em detalhe.

items.note: Ajuste refinado de entonação: pequenas variações de altura e de ritmo mudam a atitude (cortesia, ironia, reserva, compromisso) sem mudar as palavras.
words: I suppose that’s one way to put it. ↘↗ (reserva)
Well, that’s ONE way to put it. ↘ (ironia)

prompts.model: She was born in 1906 near Hanover.

prompts.q: Link two actions with a participle.
prompts.model: Completing her doctorate, she left Germany.
Her book, which appeared in 1951, made her name.

blocks.task: Write a 6-sentence mini-biography of a thinker you admire, with birth, key events and legacy.
blocks.model: Simone Weil was born in Paris in 1909. She studied philosophy and taught at several schools. Working in a factory, she wrote about labour and dignity. She left France in 1942 and died in England in 1943. Her essays, which were published after her death, have influenced many readers. Her legacy has not faded.

body: Treine esta habilidade com o formato de tarefas curtas das provas (TOEFL/IELTS).
Leia o enunciado primeiro e procure as palavras-chave.
Use exemplos reais da vida dos alunos e peça frases próprias.
Corrija o erro mais frequente da aula em grupo, sem expor o aluno.
Retome o conteúdo na aula seguinte com um exercício curto.
